title: P6 step 2: the exact numeric core of the VectorDB family (rholang/src/rust/interpreter/tensor) and its Rocq model Similarity.v.
design: P6 design v3 (.reified-rspaces-work/p6/design-v3.md), sections 4.1, 4.4 and 5. The headline ids are the ids of the P6 phase of formal/reified-rspaces-invariant-map.json.
code_base: The items are in the P6 step 2 commit of this repository. The line numbers are informative. The checker finds each item by its scope and name.

S1.name: cosine_squared_form_iff
S1.statement: In every ordered commutative ring, the real numbers included: for s = |q|·|e| > 0, t·s ≤ q·e (cos ≥ t) holds exactly when cosine_within(q·e, t, s·s), the decision of within, which uses no root.

S2.name: cosine_order_squared_form
S2.statement: With s_i·s_i = |q|²·|e_i|², the real order cos_1 ≤ cos_2 holds exactly when cosine_le, the order of better, which cross-multiplies the squares by the norms of the other record.

S3.name: euclidean_radius_squared_form
S3.statement: For a distance d ≥ 0, d ≤ r holds exactly when euclidean_within(d², r): r ≥ 0 and d² ≤ r².

S4.name: threshold_monotone
S4.statement: A lower threshold admits every record that a higher threshold admits, under cosine, dot and jaccard.

S5.name: radius_monotone
S5.statement: A larger radius admits every record that a smaller radius admits, under euclidean, manhattan and hamming.

S6.name: dot_laws
S6.statement: The dot product is symmetric, and its exact sum does not depend on the order of the coordinates.

S7.name: distance_laws
S7.statement: dist2 is non-negative, symmetric and zero exactly on equal vectors; manhattan is non-negative, symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality.

S9.name: cosine_bounds
S9.statement: Every record passes the cosine threshold −1, and no record passes a threshold above 1.

S10.name: score_orders_total
S10.statement: The order of each of the six metrics is a total preorder on its scores: cosine over positive record norms, dot and the distances by their values, jaccard over positive unions.

S11.name: squared_forms_embed
S11.statement: An embedding of ordered rings keeps the decisions of S1 to S3, so the decisions in the rationals are the decisions in the real numbers.

S12.name: binary_laws
S12.statement: Hamming is a metric on binary vectors, the jaccard counts satisfy inter ≤ union and are symmetric, and the union is empty only when neither vector sets a position.

S13.name: selection_total_order
S13.statement: The selection order (the better score, then the lower DR-75 rank) is irreflexive, transitive and total on distinct ranks.

S14.name: topk_deterministic
S14.statement: Two sorted arrangements of one multiset of candidates are equal, so their first k candidates are equal.

S15.name: list_selection_deterministic
S15.statement: List mode, the first k eligible candidates in the selection order, depends only on the multiset of records, and the insertion sort computes it.

S16.name: kappa_dropped_not_unique
S16.statement: Negative control: by score alone, two equal-score records have two sorted arrangements with different first records.

S17.name: Qc_ordered_ring
S17.statement: The canonical rationals satisfy every hypothesis of the ordered ring of Part 1.

S18.name: similarity_headlines_Qc
S18.statement: S1, S2, S3, S8 and S9 hold in the canonical rationals.

S19.name: squared_forms_embed_Z_Qc
S19.statement: S11 holds for the embedding of the integers into the rationals.

S20.name: selection_Qc
S20.statement: S13 and S14 hold for rational scores.

items.name: new
items.role: The query of a receive: ‖q‖² for cosine (a zero query has no direction and is refused), and the bits for hamming and jaccard.

items.name: add
items.role: The exact sum of dyadic terms with the least exponent as its unit: no rounding, so the sum does not depend on the order of the terms.

items.name: dot
items.role: The exact dot product, by DYADIC-SUM or by reduced rationals.

items.name: distance2
items.role: The exact squared euclidean distance.

items.name: manhattan
items.role: The exact manhattan distance.

items.name: bits
items.role: The bits of a binary vector, or None when an element is not 0 or 1 (decision 66).

items.name: hamming
items.role: The hamming distance of two bit vectors.

items.name: jaccard
items.role: The intersection and the union of two bit vectors, or None for an empty union.

items.name: score
items.role: The exact score of a record for a query, or None when it is undefined.

items.name: better
items.role: The exact order of two scores of one query: COSINE-BETTER, the values, and the cross-multiplied jaccard ratios.

items.name: within
items.role: The exact bound decisions: the squared forms of cosine and euclidean, and the other thresholds and radii.

items.name: Candidate
items.role: A candidate of a selection: its score and its rank in the canonical order of DR-75.

items.name: selection_order
items.role: The selection order: the better score, then the lower rank (decisions 41 and 60).

items.name: rank
items.role: The metered heap sort of the candidates in the selection order.

items.name: Exact
items.role: The exact numbers of the core: reduced rationals (num_rational::BigRational), which Qc models; the property test checks the ordered ring laws that Part 5 discharges for Qc.

items.name: number_of
items.role: The exact value of every number kind: a dyadic number or a reduced rational, so every decision is a decision of the rationals.

items.name: vector_of
items.role: The exact vector of a list of numbers, with its dimension checked.

items.name: delivered
items.role: The delivered value RN_53 of an exact score.
items.unmodeled: Rocq has no IEEE-754 model (plan, formal verification). The Rust oracle tests against IEEE division and square root, the Sage leg (MPFR) and the Python receipt check it against test-vectors/numeric-reference-v1.json.

items.name: round_to_f64
items.role: RN_53 of a rational.
items.unmodeled: Rocq has no IEEE-754 model. The IEEE quotient and identity oracles, the Sage leg and the Python receipt check it.

items.name: sqrt_to_f64
items.role: RN_53 of the square root of a rational.
items.unmodeled: Rocq has no IEEE-754 model. The IEEE square root oracle, the Sage leg and the Python receipt check it.
